newsitem.title: UK: Thorn to appeal US ruling on rental-purchase.
newsitem.headline: Thorn to appeal US ruling on rental-purchase.

text.p: Britain's Thorn Plc said on Thursday it intends to appeal the decision by the U.S. district court that its rental-purchase transactions in Wisconsin should be deemed consumer credit sales.
"Thorn intends to appeal this decision at the appropriate time to the Seventh Circuit Court of Appeals," said the electronic rentals company in a statement.
Consumer credit sales are subject to consumer legislation including limits on interest rates, but Wisconsin does not have a statute that specifically governs rental-purchase transactions, said Thorn.
Rent-to-own dealerships have come under attack in the U.S. for charging allegedly excessive rates of interest.

A Thorn spokesman said throughout most of the U.S. the regulation of rental purchase is governed by state statute, but noted that a number of states have no defined legislation. "Over many years a string of litigation has come in the direction of Thorn that seeks to define our contract with our customers as a credit sale," said a company spokesman.

"The significance of this is that a credit sale in the U.S. is subject to limitiations on the APR (annualised percentage rate), which pay no respect to the fact that Thorn is offering a lot of additional flexibility and services that go with a rental contract."
Thorn said should the appeal prove ultimately unsuccessful, it would not expect damages to be "material to shareholders' funds."
The company said that a similar case in Minnesota, involving a different set of facts and a different statute is on appeal before the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals.
Thorn said it may appeal any adverse decision to the United States Supreme Court.
The group has 23 and 8 stores in Wisconsin and Minnesota respectively, out of a total of over 1,300 company-owned stores throughout the United States.
